end.summary:
Myra practised recognising that a moved or turned shape keeps the same size and shape on a grid.
They used sides, corners, right angles, and a cycle-turning analogy to explain this.
They mixed up dots, gaps, and jumps; the dots-to-gaps count was corrected in turn 10, but the idea still needs checking next time.
Teach-back was not passed; further practice is needed with grid distances and turns.
end.parentNote: Asha practised turning and moving shapes on a grid with Myra. Myra used the useful method of checking side lengths and corners, and their dots-versus-gaps mix-up was corrected later by counting the jumps between dots; this still needs checking next time. At home, try drawing four dots in a row and ask Myra to count both the dots and the gaps before turning the paper.
